speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and did you experience any recent injury or bite to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any immediate deformity or inability to bend or straighten the finger at the time of injury? Are you experiencing significant bruising or tenderness over the joint or bone?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: You are describing the classic signs of a "jersey finger" injury, which is an avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. I need to confirm that you cannot actively bend the very last joint of your finger when holding your wrist in a neutral position. REQUEST TEST: MRI_hand_wrist

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI is normal, let's look at the X-ray to rule out a bony avulsion fracture. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_right_hand

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray_of_the_Right_Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal MRI and X-ray results, we must reconsider the tendon injury. Can you confirm if you are unable to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint, or if you can flex it but it is just painful? Also, is there any tenderness specifically at the base of the fingernail where the tendon attaches?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you confirm if you are completely unable to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint, or is the motion just painful? Also, do you feel a gap or lump at the base of your fingernail where the tendon attaches?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the normal imaging, your inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint after a forced extension injury is clinically diagnostic of a Flexor Digitorum Profundus avulsion, commonly known as Jersey finger. DIAGNOSIS READY: Flexor Digitorum Profundus Avulsion (Jersey Finger)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
